Subject: Opslytics renewal kickoff — staged upgrade ask

Team,

Opslytics (Alex Turner / Priya) kicked off renewal conversation this morning. They are currently on a 16-GPU reserved pool (monthly committed hours) and are asking for a path to 32 GPUs at renewal. Key constraints: they need stronger throughput SLO language for inference 95th p99 windows during business hours, and they want blended per-hour reserved pricing for the first 3 months of the staged upgrade.

Goals for our response:
- Provide a staged commitment model (16 -> 24 for 1 month -> 32 thereafter) to reduce their immediate spend while giving us runway to provision (they want gradual onboarding).
- Offer a discounted per-hour reserved rate for the first 90 days (blended), and then a sustained reserved rate after that.
- Include a throughput guardrail (p95 token latency & throughput target) with an ops playbook and an auto-burst fallback to hosted for spikes.

Can you pull the latest utilization profile and a recommended blended rate (3-month staged discount) by EOD tomorrow? Also I want SRE language for the throughput SLA/rollback triggers so we can present an achievable commitment.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Renewal: staged capacity increase & revised reserved-hour pricing for Opslytics

Alex / Priya —

Great speaking with you earlier. Per our call, attached is a short proposal that lays out a staged upgrade path from your current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 32-GPU pool over a 90-day window. High-level summary:

- Stage A (Month 0-1): 16 GPUs + incremental 8 GPUs (24 total) on a 30-day trial of blended reserved hours. Blended reserved rate applies for first 30 days to help smoothing.
- Stage B (Month 2-3): Move to full 32-GPU reserved pool with a 90-day reduced per-hour rate (blended for months 2-3).
- Post 90 days: Sustained reserved per-hour rate (listed in attached pricing sheet).

Throughput & reliability commitments:
- We will guarantee baseline sustained throughput for your typical workload (based on the profile you shared) with a p95 latency target for inference under normal business-hour load. If we miss the target for two consecutive weekly windows, we will trigger a capacity remediation plan (priority scheduling + temporary host-based burst) and credit 5% of the monthly reserved fee for that week.

Next steps:
1) Review attached Opslytics_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf and reserved_hours_pricing_v2.xlsx.
2) Confirm whether Opslytics is comfortable with the staged schedule above and the proposed 90-day blended pricing window. If yes, we will generate an MOU and send to contracts for a 30-day signature turnaround.

We aimed to be pragmatic on the blended pricing while protecting availability for existing customers. If you'd like, Rishi and Dev can jump on a short call next week to walk the SRE mitigations and capacity timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Opslytics_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal summary), reserved_hours_pricing_v2.xlsx (detailed rate card)

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: staged capacity increase & revised reserved-hour pricing for Opslytics

Marissa —

Thanks for the proposal and the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from our side after reviewing with engineering and finance:

1) Pricing: The blended 90-day approach is reasonable, but finance pushed back on the per-hour blended level in month 2 — they want a clearer floor for months 2-3 (i.e., a maximum blended effective rate). Can you provide a binding blended cap?

2) Throughput SLA: We appreciate the remediation plan, but ops needs an explicit throughput guarantee in concrete units (tokens/sec or inferences/sec) for the standard model they run (ResNet-variant). Can you map your p95 latency target to a tokens/sec metric based on their workload? If you can’t guarantee tokens/sec, we need stronger burst fallback (longer auto-host burst) or a larger safety buffer during Stage A.

3) Contract timing: We prefer the MOU before we route to procurement. Can you send one with the blended cap added and a simple acceptance section?

If you can get those items by EOD Wednesday, we’ll do an internal exec review Thursday and aim to sign the MOU Friday.

Best,
Alex Turner
Head of Infrastructure, Opslytics
alex.turner@opslytics.ai

Alex —

Thanks for the clear notes — all good and actionable. Answers inline below and attached an updated pricing spreadsheet with a capped blended rate for months 2-3 (see reserved_hours_pricing_v2.xlsx, tab "BlendedCap").

1) Blended cap: We populated a binding maximum effective blended per-hour rate for months 2-3 in the updated sheet. This is reflected as a "blended cap" row and will be called out in the MOU.

2) Throughput SLA mapping: Dev ran your workload sample against our staging harness and produced a tokens/sec mapping for the ResNet variant at your typical batch sizes. Short summary: baseline sustained throughput = 1,200 inferences/sec (avg) with p95 latency <= 220ms for the model under the tested batch distribution. We will include these numbers in the MOU and in the Ops playbook. If we fall below p95 for two consecutive weekly windows, the remediation plan and credit described earlier applies. If you prefer a stronger burst fallback we can extend the host-burst window from 15 minutes to 45 minutes for Stage A.

3) MOU: Attached is a one-page MOU draft that includes the blended cap and the throughput numbers. If that looks good, indicate "Accepted" and we’ll route to contracts for signature.

We are flexible on the exact burst length if you want a compromise (e.g., 30-minute burst + a 3% additional safety credit). Let me know which you prefer and I’ll update the MOU accordingly.

Thanks — can we target EOD Thursday for your acceptance so Contracts can kick?

Regards,
